note: What the exam is and how it is built. Everything here describes the shape of the paper, not the result: this app does not say whether you passed, does not predict a score, and is not affiliated with HRD Korea or the EPS programme. Where a number changes from round to round it is named as such rather than written down.

sections.title: What the paper is
body: The EPS-TOPIK is the Korean test taken to enter the Employment Permit System — the route by which workers from the sending countries come to Korea on an E-9 visa. It is not the academic TOPIK and the two do not substitute for each other.
The paper is forty questions in fifty minutes: twenty listening (듣기) and twenty reading (읽기), twenty-five minutes each. It is sat on a computer or a tablet rather than on paper.

What it tests is stated plainly by HRD Korea: everyday Korean, the Korean you need in industry, and an understanding of how a Korean workplace works. That is why so much of the vocabulary is about shifts, wages, safety signs and the clinic.

sections.title: The job-related questions
body: Some of the questions are drawn from one of eight job groups rather than from the common pool. Which group is not a choice you make in the exam room: you pick it when you apply, and every job-related question on your paper comes from that one.

This only applies to people applying for manufacturing work. An applicant for agriculture, fishing, construction or service work gets common questions in place of them — so if that is you, the trades section here is optional reading rather than something you have to revise.

The eight groups are 고무·플라스틱, 전기·전자, 금속·재료, 기계·금형, 식품가공, 섬유·의복, 화학·제약 and 펄프·종이·목재. HRD Korea publishes the job-related question bank in advance, which is unusual and worth knowing: those questions are meant to be studied rather than guessed at.
The Special EPS-TOPIK — the round for former workers returning to Korea — carries a larger share of job-related questions than the ordinary round does.

sections.title: The question shapes
body: Listening opens with pictures: you hear a word or a sentence and choose the drawing that matches. Then short exchanges — someone says one line and you pick the natural reply — and then conversations of two to four turns with a question about what was said or what has to be done.

Reading opens the same way, with a picture or a sign: 출입 금지, 손 조심, 안전모 착용. Then vocabulary and grammar in a gapped sentence, then 'choose the sentence that means the same', then a notice or a short passage with two or three questions hanging off it.

The passages are workplace documents more often than they are stories: a shift notice, a health-check announcement, a set of safety rules, a contract. Reading one quickly is a skill of its own and it is most of what the second half of the reading paper asks for.

sections.title: Marking, and what this app will not tell you
body: Each question carries equal weight and the two halves are worth the same as each other.

This app does not tell you whether a practice score is a pass. The cut score is set per round and differs by industry, and the number of people taking it changes what it lands on — so any pass mark written into an app is a number invented to sound useful.
What a practice paper here does give you is the list of questions you got wrong, with the reason. That is the part worth acting on.
For anything official — dates, eligibility, results, what your own cut score was — go to HRD Korea's own EPS-TOPIK site. This app has no connection to them and does not know your registration.

sections.title: How to use the fifty minutes
body: The clock does not stop between sections in practice here, and running out of time is a more common way to lose marks than not knowing the answer.
In listening you hear each item on its own schedule, so the discipline is to decide and move on: a question you are still weighing when the next one starts costs you two, not one.
In reading, the passages are at the end and take the longest. Getting to them with ten minutes left is worth more than getting every gap-fill right.
Answer everything. Nothing is deducted for a wrong answer, so a blank is strictly worse than a guess.
The practice paper in this app is deliberately unforgiving about this — it marks nothing until you hand it in, because finding out at the end is the thing you are practising for.

sections.title: What actually moves the score
body: Signs and notices. They are free marks, there are a limited number of them in ordinary use, and they turn up in both halves of the paper. The 유형별 drills in this app start here for that reason.
Numbers and time. Hours, dates, wages, quantities — Korean runs two number systems and the exam leans on the join between them. Mishearing 두 시 for 열두 시 costs a question you otherwise understood.

The formal register. The paper is written in -습니다/-십시오 throughout. If the Korean you hear at work is casual, the exam's register will feel oddly stiff, and that unfamiliarity is worth practising away.
Your own trade's vocabulary, if you are applying for manufacturing work. It is a small, closed list and it is published in advance.
Little and often beats a long session. The review deck here exists for that: it brings back what you got wrong at widening gaps, which is the one study habit with good evidence behind it.
